import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An opaque set for a planar set meets every straight line which meets that set. The opaque forest
problem asks how short an opaque set can be for various planar shapes.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Opaque forest problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- A. Dumitrescu, M. Jiang, and J. Pach, *Opaque sets*, Algorithmica 69 (2014), 315–334.
- J. S. Provan, M. Brazil, D. A. Thomas, and J. F. Weng,
  *Minimum opaque covers for polygonal regions*, Algorithmica 70 (2014), 316–344.
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/-- A set `B` is opaque for `K` if every straight line that meets `K` also meets `B`. -/
def IsOpaque (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : ℝ², p ≠ q →
    ((line[ℝ, p, q] : Set ℝ²) ∩ K).Nonempty →
    ((line[ℝ, p, q] : Set ℝ²) ∩ B).Nonempty

/-- A graphical opaque forest is a set which is the union of finitely many line segments. -/
def IsSegmentForest (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ p q : Fin n → ℝ², B = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (p i) (q i)

/--
The infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of unrestricted opaque sets for the unit
square is conjectured to be $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}/2$, the length of the Jones--Poirier
two-component forest. The opaque set need not lie in the square and need not be connected.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    let square : Set ℝ² := convexHull ℝ
      {!₂[(0 : ℝ), 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]}
    IsGLB {L : ENNReal | ∃ B : Set ℝ², IsOpaque square B ∧ μH[1] B = L}
      (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 + Real.sqrt 6 / 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that every compact convex set in the plane with nonempty interior has a shortest
opaque set? A positive answer means that some unrestricted opaque set attains the least
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure among all opaque sets for each such convex set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →
        ∃ B : Set ℝ², IsOpaque K B ∧
          IsLeast {L : ENNReal | ∃ A : Set ℝ², IsOpaque K A ∧ μH[1] A = L} (μH[1] B) := by
  sorry

/--
The Graphical Conjecture: for every convex polygon there is a finite union of straight-line
segments which is opaque for the polygonal region and has minimum one-dimensional Hausdorff
measure among all unrestricted opaque sets for that region. Here “graphical” means only a finite
union of segments; no acyclicity condition is imposed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin n → ℝ²), 3 ≤ n → IsConvexPolygon p →
      let K : Set ℝ² := convexHull ℝ (Set.range p)
      ∃ B : Set ℝ², IsSegmentForest B ∧ IsOpaque K B ∧
        IsLeast {L : ENNReal | ∃ A : Set ℝ², IsOpaque K A ∧ μH[1] A = L} (μH[1] B) := by
  sorry

/--
For a unit equilateral triangle, the infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of
unrestricted opaque sets is conjectured to equal $\sqrt{3}$, the length of its minimum Steiner
tree. No connectivity assumption is imposed on the opaque sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle :
    ∀ t : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ², t.Equilateral → dist (t.points 0) (t.points 1) = 1 →
      IsGLB {L : ENNReal | ∃ B : Set ℝ²,
        IsOpaque (convexHull ℝ (Set.range t.points)) B ∧ μH[1] B = L}
        (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem
modeling_decisions: An opaque set is modeled by quantifying over all nondegenerate affine lines, represented as the affine span of two distinct planar points; a barrier may be any set anywhere in the plane.
Length is Mathlib's normalized one-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1]`, valued in `ENNReal`. No measurability, rectifiability, connectivity, or location restriction is imposed on general barriers.
The unit square is the convex hull of the four standard vertices `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,1)`, and `(0,1)`.
The minimizer-existence variant is encoded as a yes/no question using `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`, since the source does not assert that the positive answer is specifically conjectured.
A convex polygonal region is represented as the convex hull of the range of a cyclic vertex map satisfying the repository's `IsConvexPolygon` predicate, with at least three vertices.

For the Graphical Conjecture, “graphical” is interpreted according to Provan–Brazil–Thomas–Weng as a finite union of line segments. No graph-theoretic acyclicity requirement is imposed. Its graphical witness is required to minimize length against all opaque sets, not only finite segment unions.

The unit equilateral-triangle statement quantifies over affine triangles that are equilateral and have one side of length one; the target region is the convex hull of their vertices. This coordinate-free formulation covers every unit equilateral triangle.
Infimum claims use `IsGLB`; only the two existence variants use `IsLeast`, so the square and triangle statements do not assert that a minimizer exists.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An *opaque set* (also called a barrier, beam detector or opaque cover) for a set $K$ in the
plane is a set $S$ that meets every line meeting $K$. The opaque forest problem asks for the
shortest opaque set of a given planar shape, where length is measured by the one-dimensional
Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$. The barrier is not restricted in location (it may lie
outside $K$) and need not be connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [DJP14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M. and Pach, J., *Opaque sets*. Algorithmica 69 (2014),
  315-334. [arXiv:1005.2218](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A. and Jiang, M., *The opaque square*. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on
  Computational Geometry (SoCG'14). [arXiv:1311.3323](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3323)
- [PBTW12] Provan, J. S., Brazil, M., Thomas, D. A. and Weng, J. F., *Minimum opaque covers for
  polygonal regions*. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
- [Iz16] Izumi, T., *Improving the lower bound on opaque sets for equilateral triangle*.
  Discrete Applied Mathematics 213 (2016), 130-138.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal EuclideanGeometry

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/--
`S` is an *opaque set* (barrier, beam detector, opaque cover) for `K`: every line in the plane
that meets `K` also meets `S`. Lines are the affine subspaces of `ℝ²` with one-dimensional
direction. No restriction is placed on the location or connectivity of `S`.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K S : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    (K ∩ L).Nonempty → (S ∩ L).Nonempty

/--
The *shortest opaque length* of `K`: the infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure
$\mathcal{H}^1(S)$ over all opaque sets `S` for `K` (as an extended nonnegative real).
This infimum need not be attained, see `opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists`.
-/
noncomputable def opaqueLength (K : Set ℝ²) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (S : Set ℝ²) (_ : IsOpaqueSet K S), μH[1] S

/--
`S` is *graphical* in the sense of [PBTW12]: it is the union of finitely many (closed) line
segments. Opaque graphical sets are the *opaque forests* of the Wikipedia article. We do not
impose acyclicity: a shortest graphical opaque set never contains a cycle, since deleting a
piece of a cycle keeps the component connected and hence keeps the blocked lines unchanged.
-/
def IsGraphical (S : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ E : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), S = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- The closed unit square $[0, 1]^2$. -/
def unitSquare : Set ℝ² :=
  convexHull ℝ {!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]}

/-- The closed equilateral triangle with unit side length. -/
noncomputable def unitEquilateralTriangle : Set ℝ² :=
  convexHull ℝ {!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1 / 2, √3 / 2]}

/-- Every set is an opaque set for itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isOpaqueSet_self (K : Set ℝ²) : IsOpaqueSet K K :=
  fun _ _ h => h

/-- Enlarging an opaque set keeps it opaque. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem IsOpaqueSet.mono {K S T : Set ℝ²} (hS : IsOpaqueSet K S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
    IsOpaqueSet K T :=
  fun L hL hK => (hS L hL hK).mono (Set.inter_subset_inter_left _ hST)

/-- The shortest opaque length of `K` is at most the length of `K` itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem opaqueLength_le (K : Set ℝ²) : opaqueLength K ≤ μH[1] K :=
  iInf₂_le K (isOpaqueSet_self K)

/-- The empty set has a shortest opaque set, namely the empty set. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem opaqueLength_empty : opaqueLength ∅ = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (zero_le _)
  simpa using opaqueLength_le ∅

/-- A single line segment is graphical. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isGraphical_segment (a b : ℝ²) : IsGraphical (segment ℝ a b) :=
  ⟨{(a, b)}, by simp⟩

/--
**The opaque forest problem for the unit square.** The boundary of the unit square is an
opaque set of length $4$, and a shorter opaque forest of length
$\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} \approx 2.639$ is known: the minimum Steiner tree of three
vertices of the square together with a segment joining the fourth vertex to the centre
(Jones 1962, 1964; Poirier). It is conjectured that this forest is optimal, i.e. that the
infimum of the lengths of all opaque sets for the unit square, with no restriction on location
or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$. This is unproven: the best known
lower bound is only $2.00002$ for barriers made of countably many rectifiable curves.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    opaqueLength unitSquare = ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2) := by
  sorry

/--
It is not known whether every convex set has a shortest opaque set, or whether instead the
lengths of its opaque sets might approach an infimum without ever reaching it. Here the
convex set is a convex body: a compact convex subset of the plane with nonempty interior
(the degenerate cases of points and segments are excluded), and the opaque sets are arbitrary
subsets of the plane measured by $\mathcal{H}^1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ S, IsOpaqueSet K S ∧ μH[1] S = opaqueLength K := by
  sorry

/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12]: every convex polygon
has an opaque forest as its shortest opaque set. That is, for every convex polygonal region
(the convex hull of finitely many points with nonempty interior) there is an opaque set which is
a finite union of line segments and whose length equals the infimum of the lengths of all
opaque sets for the region. In particular the infimum is attained.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture
    (V : Finset ℝ²) (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ S, IsGraphical S ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) S ∧
      μH[1] S = opaqueLength (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) := by
  sorry

/--
For a triangle the shortest *connected* opaque set is its minimum Steiner tree, but without
assuming connectivity the optimality of the Steiner tree has not been demonstrated, even for
the equilateral triangle ([DJP14], [Iz16]). For the equilateral triangle with unit side the
Steiner tree consists of the three segments from the vertices to the centre and has length
$\sqrt{3}$. The conjecture is that the infimum of the lengths of all opaque sets for the unit
equilateral triangle, with no restriction on location or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle :
    opaqueLength unitEquilateralTriangle = ENNReal.ofReal √3 := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem
attempts.decomposition_objections: Minor: the equilateral_triangle slot notes say the arbitrary-triangle version 'is not clearly asserted as a conjecture anywhere', but Provan–Brazil–Thomas–Weng (arXiv:1210.8139, Conclusion, open question 1) explicitly conjecture that the minimum graphical opaque cover of ANY triangular region is the minimum Steiner tree of its vertices (proved by them for at most two components). I conformed to the table and stated only the equilateral case (infimum over unrestricted opaque sets equals √3), but a general-triangle variant (for graphical opaque sets) would be faithful to the literature. Also, the Wikipedia sentence 'for most other shapes this problem similarly remains unsolved' was correctly dropped.
modeling_decisions: Length is the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1]` on `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (Euclidean metric), valued in ℝ≥0∞; conjectured constants are entered via `ENNReal.ofReal`. The infimum `opaqueLength` is taken over ALL subsets of the plane (not just forests), matching the slot notes; since any opaque set can be approximated in length by forests the infimum is the same either way.

A 'line' is an `AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²` whose direction has finrank 1; 'S is opaque for K' means every such line meeting K meets S (equivalent to K ⊆ coverage(S)). No interior/exterior/connectivity restriction is imposed, as the article says is the default.

Slot 1 and slot 4 are stated as infimum equalities (not attained minima), per the notes; because the candidate forests attain the stated lengths, each equality is equivalent to the conjectured lower bound.

Slot 2: 'every convex set' is read as every compact convex set with nonempty interior (convex body), per the notes. Degenerate cases (points, segments) trivially have minimizers, so this restriction does not change the truth value; unbounded sets are excluded as the article's problem concerns bounded convex sets.

Slot 3: 'opaque forest' is formalized as a finite union of closed segments (`IsGraphical`, the sources' 'graphical') without requiring acyclicity. A minimum-length graphical opaque set can contain no cycle (removing a piece of a cycle edge preserves the component's connectivity, hence its convex hull and blocked lines, while shortening it), so the two readings are equivalent for minimizers. The statement uses the existential reading (there exists a minimizer that is graphical), following Wikipedia's 'has an opaque forest as its shortest opaque set'; PBTW's 'a minimum OC is always graphical' could also be read as universal over minimizers.
Slot 3: 'convex polygon' is the convex hull of a Finset of points in ℝ² with nonempty interior (excluding degenerate polygons, for which the conjecture is trivially true).
Slot 4: the unit equilateral triangle is placed with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1/2, √3/2); the candidate value √3 is the length of its minimum Steiner tree (3 · 1/√3).

Several short `@[category API]`/`@[category test]` lemmas with proofs are included to check the bespoke definitions (self-opacity, monotonicity, `opaqueLength ∅ = 0`, segments are graphical), as CONTRIBUTING.md requests basic API tests for bespoke definitions.

- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _The opaque square_. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on

  polygonal regions_. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
- [Iz16] Izumi, T., _Improving the lower bound on opaque sets for equilateral triangle_.

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/--
A set `B` in the plane is an *opaque set* (or *barrier*) for the set `K` if every line in the
plane that meets `K` also meets `B`. A line is an affine subspace of `ℝ²` whose direction is
one-dimensional. No restriction is placed on the location of `B`: it may lie outside `K` and it
need not be connected.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    (K ∩ L).Nonempty → (B ∩ L).Nonempty

/--
The set of lengths of all opaque sets for `K`, where the length of an arbitrary set is its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$ (which agrees with the usual length for line
segments and rectifiable curves).
-/
noncomputable def opaqueLengths (K : Set ℝ²) : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] '' {B | IsOpaqueSet K B}

/-- A set is a *finite union of line segments* if it is the union of finitely many (closed)
line segments. Following [PBTW12], such opaque sets are called *graphical*. -/
def IsFiniteUnionOfSegments (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), B = ⋃ e ∈ S, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

  fun _ _ h => h

theorem IsOpaqueSet.mono {K B B' : Set ℝ²} (h : IsOpaqueSet K B) (hB : B ⊆ B') :

**Existence of a shortest opaque set.**
Does every convex body $K$ in the plane (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) have a
shortest opaque set? That is, is there an opaque set for $K$ whose length
($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set for $K$? The
alternative is that the lengths of the opaque sets for $K$ approach their infimum without ever
reaching it. The opaque sets range over arbitrary subsets of the plane, measured by
$\mathcal{H}^1$, and are unrestricted in location.

theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →

  sorry

**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].
Every convex polygon (the convex hull of finitely many points of the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. a finite union of line segments.

($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) is at most the length of every other opaque set for the polygon.

could be removed without unblocking any line, so requiring the union to be a forest gives an
equivalent statement.

  sorry

equilateral triangle of side length $1$ this tree consists of the three segments from the
vertices to the centre and has length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the
optimality of the Steiner tree has not been demonstrated: the conjecture is that the infimum of

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An *opaque set* (also called a barrier, beam detector or opaque cover) for a set $K$ in the
plane is a set $B$ that meets every line meeting $K$. The opaque forest problem asks for the
opaque set of minimum length, where the length of an arbitrary set is its one-dimensional
Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$. The barrier is not restricted in location and need not be
connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Opaque forest problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- [Wikipedia list entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [DJP14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M. and Pach, J., *Opaque sets*. Algorithmica 69 (2014),
  315–334. [arXiv:1005.2218](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A. and Jiang, M., *The opaque square*. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on
  Computational Geometry (SoCG'14). [arXiv:1311.3323](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3323)
- [PBTW12] Provan, J. S., Brazil, M., Thomas, D. A. and Weng, J. F., *Minimum opaque covers for
  polygonal regions*. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/--
`B` is an *opaque set* (or *barrier*) for `K`: every line in the plane that meets `K` also
meets `B`. Lines are affine subspaces of `ℝ²` with one-dimensional direction. No restriction is
placed on the location of `B`; in particular `B` may lie partly or entirely outside `K` and
need not be connected.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ K).Nonempty → ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ B).Nonempty

/--
The set of lengths of all opaque sets for `K`, where the length of an arbitrary set is its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$ (which agrees with the usual length for
segments and rectifiable curves).
-/
def opaqueLengths (K : Set ℝ²) : Set ℝ≥0∞ :=
  {μH[1] B | (B : Set ℝ²) (_ : IsOpaqueSet K B)}

/--
`B` is a finite union of (closed) line segments in the plane. In [PBTW12] such sets are called
*graphical*. An opaque set of this form is an *opaque forest*; Wikipedia additionally asks the
union of the segments to be acyclic, which is automatic for an opaque set of minimum length of
this form, so it is not required here.
-/
def IsFiniteSegmentUnion (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ E : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), B = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- The closed unit square $[0, 1]^2$ in the plane. -/
def unitSquare : Set ℝ² :=
  {x | x 0 ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ x 1 ∈ Set.Icc 0 1}

/--
**Opaque forest problem** for the unit square.

The shortest known opaque set for the unit square has length
$\sqrt{2} + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \approx 2.639$: it consists of the minimum Steiner tree of three
of the vertices of the square together with a segment from the fourth vertex to the centre
(Jones 1962/1964, rediscovered by Poirier). It is conjectured to be optimal [DJP14, DJ14], i.e.
the infimum of the $\mathcal{H}^1$-length over all opaque sets for the unit square (with no
restriction on their location or connectivity) equals $\sqrt{2} + \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$. This is
stated as an infimum rather than a minimum since it is not known whether a shortest opaque set
exists.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths unitSquare) (ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Does every convex body in the plane have a shortest opaque set? That is, for every compact
convex set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with nonempty interior, is the infimum of the
$\mathcal{H}^1$-length over all opaque sets for $K$ attained by some opaque set? It is not known
whether this holds, or whether instead the lengths of the opaque sets might approach the
infimum without ever reaching it.

The restriction to nonempty interior excludes degenerate convex bodies (points and segments),
for which the body itself is trivially a shortest opaque set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : ConvexBody ℝ², (interior (K : Set ℝ²)).Nonempty →
      ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ IsLeast (opaqueLengths K) (μH[1] B) := by
  sorry

/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** [PBTW12]: every convex polygon has an opaque forest as its
shortest opaque set. That is, if $K$ is a convex polygonal region (the convex hull of finitely
many points, with nonempty interior), then there is a finite union of line segments that is an
opaque set for $K$ and whose $\mathcal{H}^1$-length is the minimum length over all opaque sets
for $K$ (which need not be connected, measurable, or contained in $K$). In particular this
would imply that convex polygons have shortest opaque sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture (S : Finset ℝ²)
    (hS : (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsFiniteSegmentUnion B ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)) B ∧
      IsLeast (opaqueLengths (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ²))) (μH[1] B) := by
  sorry

/--
For a triangle, the shortest *connected* opaque set is its minimum Steiner tree; for an
equilateral triangle of side $1$ this tree joins the three vertices to the centre and has
length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the optimality of the Steiner tree has not
been demonstrated [DJP14, PBTW12]. The conjecture states that the infimum of the
$\mathcal{H}^1$-length over all (not necessarily connected, unrestricted) opaque sets for a unit
equilateral triangle equals $\sqrt{3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle (a b c : ℝ²)
    (hab : dist a b = 1) (hbc : dist b c = 1) (hca : dist c a = 1) :
    IsGLB (opaqueLengths (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c})) (ENNReal.ofReal √3) := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem

I conformed to the table and stated only the unit equilateral triangle case (infimum = √3). Otherwise the table is consistent with the sources.
modeling_decisions: Lines are modelled as `AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²` with `Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1`; an opaque set must meet every such line meeting K (Bagemihl/DJP/PBTW definition). No measurability, connectivity, or location restriction is imposed on barriers, matching the 'unrestricted' problem.

Length is the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1]` in ℝ≥0∞ (Mathlib's normalisation gives `μH[1] (segment ℝ x y) = edist x y`, so it agrees with ordinary length). Infima/minima are taken in ℝ≥0∞ so that sets of infinite length are correctly treated as long, not as length 0.

The square conjecture and the equilateral-triangle conjecture are stated as `IsGLB` (infimum equality) rather than attained minima, since existence of a minimiser is itself open (slot minimizer_exists). The infimum is over arbitrary sets, not just forests; by DJP14 Lemma 1 / PBTW12 Lemma 2 the two infima agree.

The unit square is fixed as the axis-parallel closed square [0,1]²; the equilateral triangle is any convex hull of three points at pairwise distance 1. Both are legitimate by isometry-invariance of lines and of μH[1].

minimizer_exists: 'every convex set' is read as every planar convex body (`ConvexBody ℝ²`: compact, convex, nonempty) with nonempty interior, following the literature's 'convex body'. Degenerate bodies (points, segments) are excluded; for them the body itself is trivially a shortest opaque set, so the exclusion does not change the truth value but matches the sources. Formulated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`, the repo's yes/no idiom.

graphical_conjecture: 'convex polygon' is the convex hull of a `Finset ℝ²` with nonempty interior. 'Opaque forest' is taken as a finite union of closed segments (PBTW's 'graphical'), without requiring acyclicity: a minimum-length finite union of segments that is opaque cannot contain a cycle (removing a small piece of an edge bounding a bounded face preserves opacity and shortens it), so the statement is equivalent to the acyclic version. The conjecture is stated existentially (there is a graphical opaque set achieving the minimum over all opaque sets), following Wikipedia's phrasing and the decomposition notes, rather than PBTW's literal universal 'every minimum OC is graphical', which would be vacuous if no minimiser existed.

In the graphical conjecture, `IsOpaqueSet K B` is stated explicitly alongside `IsLeast (opaqueLengths K) (μH[1] B)` because `IsLeast` membership only guarantees some opaque set of the same length, not that B itself is opaque.

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An opaque set for a planar body meets every straight line that meets the body. The opaque
forest problem asks for opaque sets of least possible one-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Opaque forest problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- [Provan, Brazil, Thomas, and Weng, *Minimum opaque covers for polygonal regions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
- [Dumitrescu, Jiang, Pach, and Tóth, *Opaque sets*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry
open scoped MeasureTheory
open Set ENNReal

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/-- A set `B` is opaque for `K` if every complete affine line meeting `K` also meets `B`. -/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ p q : ℝ², p ≠ q →
    (((affineSpan ℝ {p, q} : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) : Set ℝ²) ∩ K).Nonempty →
    (((affineSpan ℝ {p, q} : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) : Set ℝ²) ∩ B).Nonempty

/-- The axis-aligned unit square in the Euclidean plane. -/
def unitSquare : Set ℝ² :=
  {x | ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ 1}


/-- A segment forest is a finite union of closed straight-line segments.
No graph-theoretic acyclicity condition is imposed. -/
def IsSegmentForest (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ edges : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), B = ⋃ e ∈ edges, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/--
**Opaque forest problem for the square.**

The infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of unrestricted opaque sets for the
unit square is $\sqrt{2}+\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$, the length of the Jones--Poirier
two-component forest. The opaque set need not lie in the square and need not be connected.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    IsGLB {L : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ B : Set ℝ²,
      IsOpaqueSet unitSquare B ∧ μH[1] B = L}
      (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 2 + Real.sqrt 6 / 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Existence of shortest opaque sets.**

Is it true that every compact convex planar set with nonempty interior has an unrestricted
opaque set whose one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is no greater than that of every other
opaque set for it? This asks whether the infimum is always attained, and permits arbitrary
sets as barriers.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ B : Set ℝ², IsOpaqueSet K B ∧
        ∀ B' : Set ℝ², IsOpaqueSet K B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry

/--
**Graphical Conjecture.**

Every convex polygon with nonempty interior has a globally shortest unrestricted opaque set
that is a finite union of straight-line segments. Here “graphical” means only a finite union
of segments; it does not require the resulting embedded graph to be acyclic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture :
    ∀ V : Set ℝ², V.Finite → (interior (convexHull ℝ V)).Nonempty →
      ∃ B : Set ℝ², IsSegmentForest B ∧ IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ V) B ∧
        ∀ B' : Set ℝ², IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ V) B' → μH[1] B ≤ μH[1] B' := by
  sorry

/--
**Equilateral-triangle opaque forest conjecture.**

For a unit equilateral triangle, the infimum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of
unrestricted opaque sets is $\sqrt{3}$, the length of its minimum Steiner tree. No
connectivity or location restriction is imposed on the opaque sets.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle :
    ∀ a b c : ℝ², dist a b = 1 → dist b c = 1 → dist c a = 1 →
      IsGLB {L : ℝ≥0∞ | ∃ B : Set ℝ²,
        IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c}) B ∧ μH[1] B = L}
        (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem

Used Mathlib's correctly normalized one-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1], with values in ℝ≥0∞. The square and triangle optimum claims are stated as IsGLB equalities, not attained minima.
Represented the unit square as the axis-aligned set of points whose two coordinates lie between 0 and 1.

Interpreted 'graphical' according to the primary source as a finite union of closed line segments, without imposing graph-theoretic acyclicity. Its candidate is required to minimize Hausdorff measure among all opaque sets, not merely graphical ones.

Represented a unit equilateral triangle by three planar points whose three pairwise distances are 1. Quantifying over every such triple avoids choosing coordinates while expressing the same congruence-invariant claim.
No barrier is required to lie inside the covered body or to be connected in any declaration.

/-!
# Opaque forest problem

An *opaque set* (also called a barrier, beam detector or opaque cover) for a set $K$ in the
plane is a set $B$ that meets every line meeting $K$. The opaque forest problem asks for the
shortest opaque set of a given planar shape. The length of an arbitrary set is measured by its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$, which agrees with the usual length for line
segments and rectifiable curves. Unless stated otherwise, the barrier may lie anywhere in the
plane and need not be connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opaque_forest_problem)
- [DJP14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., Pach, J., _Opaque sets_. Algorithmica 69 (2014), 315–334.
  [arXiv:1005.2218](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2218)
- [DJ14] Dumitrescu, A., Jiang, M., _The opaque square_. Proc. 30th Annual Symposium on
  Computational Geometry (SoCG'14). [arXiv:1311.3323](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3323)
- [PBTW12] Provan, J. S., Brazil, M., Thomas, D. A., Weng, J. F., _Minimum opaque covers for
  polygonal regions_. [arXiv:1210.8139](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8139)
-/

open MeasureTheory Real
open scoped ENNReal EuclideanGeometry

namespace OpaqueForestProblem

/--
A set `B` in the plane is an **opaque set** (or *barrier*) for `K` if every line in the plane
that meets `K` also meets `B`. Lines are the affine subspaces of `ℝ²` whose direction has
dimension one. No restriction is placed on the location or connectivity of `B`.
-/
def IsOpaqueSet (K B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ², Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 →
    ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ K).Nonempty → ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ B).Nonempty

/-- Every set is an opaque set for itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem isOpaqueSet_self (K : Set ℝ²) : IsOpaqueSet K K := fun _ _ h => h

/--
The infimum of the lengths of all opaque sets for `K`, where the length of an arbitrary
subset of the plane is its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1$.
-/
noncomputable def opaqueLengthInf (K : Set ℝ²) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (B : Set ℝ²) (_ : IsOpaqueSet K B), μH[1] B

/-- The length of any opaque set for `K` bounds `opaqueLengthInf K` from above. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem opaqueLengthInf_le {K B : Set ℝ²} (hB : IsOpaqueSet K B) :
    opaqueLengthInf K ≤ μH[1] B :=
  iInf₂_le B hB

/-- A set is a **finite union of line segments** if it is the union of finitely many
(closed) line segments in the plane. -/
def IsFiniteSegmentUnion (B : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²), B = ⋃ e ∈ S, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- The closed unit square $[0, 1]^2$ in the plane. -/
def unitSquare : Set ℝ² := {p | ∀ i, p i ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1}

/--
**Opaque forest problem** (for the unit square).

The shortest known opaque set for the unit square is the forest of Jones (1962, 1964) and
Poirier. It consists of the minimum Steiner tree of three of the vertices of the square
together with a line segment from the fourth vertex to the centre, and has length
$\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} \approx 2.639$. It is conjectured to be optimal: the infimum of
the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for the unit square, with no
restriction on location or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6}$.
Whether this infimum is attained is itself open, so the conjecture is stated as an equality
of infima rather than as an attained minimum.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    opaqueLengthInf unitSquare = ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2) := by
  sorry

/--
Does every convex body in the plane have a shortest opaque set?

It is not known whether every compact convex set $K$ with nonempty interior in the plane
has an opaque set whose length ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) equals the infimum of the lengths
of all its opaque sets, or whether instead the lengths of the opaque sets of some such $K$
approach the infimum without ever reaching it.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², Convex ℝ K → IsCompact K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ μH[1] B = opaqueLengthInf K := by
  sorry

/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].

Every convex polygon (the convex hull of a finite set of points in the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. composed of finitely many
straight-line segments (an opaque forest). In particular, the infimum of the lengths of the
opaque sets of a convex polygon is attained.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture
    (V : Finset ℝ²) (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B ∧ IsFiniteSegmentUnion B ∧
      μH[1] B = opaqueLengthInf (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) := by
  sorry

/--
**Opaque forest problem for the equilateral triangle.**

The shortest *connected* opaque set of a triangle is its minimum Steiner tree; for an
equilateral triangle of side $1$ this tree consists of the three segments joining the vertices
to the centre and has length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the optimality of the
Steiner tree has not been demonstrated. The conjecture is that the infimum of the lengths
($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for an equilateral triangle of side $1$, with no
restriction on location or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle
    (a b c : ℝ²) (hab : dist a b = 1) (hbc : dist b c = 1) (hca : dist c a = 1) :
    opaqueLengthInf (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c}) = ENNReal.ofReal √3 := by
  sorry

end OpaqueForestProblem

opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilater.why: For all a b c : ℝ² with pairwise distances 1, `opaqueLengthInf (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c}) = ENNReal.ofReal √3`, i.e. the infimum of H^1 over all unrestricted opaque sets of a unit equilateral triangle equals the length √3 of its Steiner tree (three radii of length 1/√3).

opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical.why: For every finite V : Finset ℝ² whose convex hull has nonempty interior (a convex polygon), there exists an opaque set B for convexHull ℝ V that is a finite union of closed segments and whose H^1-length equals the infimum over all opaque sets. This is Provan–Brazil–Thomas–Weng's Graphical Conjecture in its existential reading, and implies existence of a minimizer for polygons.

opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer.why: Yes/no question stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K, Convex ℝ K → IsCompact K → (interior K).Nonempty → ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ μH[1] B = opaqueLengthInf K`; answer(True) means every planar convex body has a shortest opaque set, answer(False) means some convex body's infimum is not attained. B ranges over arbitrary sets measured by H^1.

statement_blocks.opaque_forest_problem:
/--
**Opaque forest problem** (for the unit square).

The shortest known opaque set for the unit square is the forest of Jones (1962, 1964) and
Poirier. It consists of the minimum Steiner tree of three of the vertices of the square
together with a line segment from the fourth vertex to the centre, and has length
$\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6} \approx 2.639$. It is conjectured to be optimal: the infimum of
the lengths ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for the unit square, with no
restriction on location or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{6}$.
Whether this infimum is attained is itself open, so the conjecture is stated as an equality
of infima rather than as an attained minimum.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem :
    opaqueLengthInf unitSquare = ENNReal.ofReal (√2 + √6 / 2) := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilater:
/--
**Opaque forest problem for the equilateral triangle.**

The shortest *connected* opaque set of a triangle is its minimum Steiner tree; for an
equilateral triangle of side $1$ this tree consists of the three segments joining the vertices
to the centre and has length $\sqrt{3}$. Without assuming connectivity, the optimality of the
Steiner tree has not been demonstrated. The conjecture is that the infimum of the lengths
($\mathcal{H}^1$-measures) of all opaque sets for an equilateral triangle of side $1$, with no
restriction on location or connectivity, equals $\sqrt{3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.equilateral_triangle
    (a b c : ℝ²) (hab : dist a b = 1) (hbc : dist b c = 1) (hca : dist c a = 1) :
    opaqueLengthInf (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c}) = ENNReal.ofReal √3 := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical:
/--
**The Graphical Conjecture** of Provan, Brazil, Thomas and Weng [PBTW12].

Every convex polygon (the convex hull of a finite set of points in the plane, with nonempty
interior) has a shortest opaque set that is *graphical*, i.e. composed of finitely many
straight-line segments (an opaque forest). In particular, the infimum of the lengths of the
opaque sets of a convex polygon is attained.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.graphical_conjecture
    (V : Finset ℝ²) (hV : (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²))).Nonempty) :
    ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) B ∧ IsFiniteSegmentUnion B ∧
      μH[1] B = opaqueLengthInf (convexHull ℝ (V : Set ℝ²)) := by
  sorry
statement_blocks.opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer:
/--
Does every convex body in the plane have a shortest opaque set?

It is not known whether every compact convex set $K$ with nonempty interior in the plane
has an opaque set whose length ($\mathcal{H}^1$-measure) equals the infimum of the lengths
of all its opaque sets, or whether instead the lengths of the opaque sets of some such $K$
approach the infimum without ever reaching it.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem opaque_forest_problem.variants.minimizer_exists :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set ℝ², Convex ℝ K → IsCompact K → (interior K).Nonempty →
      ∃ B, IsOpaqueSet K B ∧ μH[1] B = opaqueLengthInf K := by
  sorry
